discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the founding of neutrino astronomy with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
motivation: Francis Halzen conceived and led IceCube, a cubic-kilometre Cherenkov detector built in the Antarctic ice, and turned it into a new window on the Universe. In 2013 IceCube discovered a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. This was the first observation of cosmic neutrinos at energies far beyond those from the Sun or SN1987A. In 2018 a real-time alert from IceCube, coincident with gamma rays from the blazar TXS 0506+056, identified a first candidate neutrino source and launched multi-messenger astronomy with neutrinos. In 2022 and 2023 IceCube found neutrino emission from NGC 1068 and mapped the Galactic plane in neutrinos. These achievements rest on bold detector design, fast real-time triggering and selection, and sophisticated data analysis. Together they opened an entirely new observational regime for physics.
